The test image shows a tomato leaf with:
- Extensive tan/brown necrosis covering most of the leaf surface
- Multiple holes/perforations where dead tissue has fallen out
- Yellowing (chlorosis) surrounding the necrotic areas
- Papery, dried texture on necrotic portions
- A younger, greener leaf nearby appears less affected

Top candidates: **Late Blight** (large irregular brown lesions), **Early Blight** (target-spot necrosis), or **Phytophthora Blight**.

Now viewing one reference image — Late Blight, my top candidate:

The Late Blight reference matches well: large irregular brown necrotic lesions spreading across the leaf with tan/papery texture and a clear boundary between diseased and (formerly) healthy tissue. The test image shows the same pattern in a more advanced stage, where the necrotic tissue has developed holes from complete tissue death and falling out. Both show extensive lesions covering most of the leaf area.
